title: Code-mode browser control: sandboxed script runtime over typed Quarry bindings, with approval-input hardening
summary: Offer the model one persistent REPL tool per session that runs model-written JS in a QuickJS/V8 isolate inside execution-core with only typed Quarry bindings (observe, act, locator, extract), no network, fs or raw CDP, memory/stack limits and a per-call deadline. Every binding call goes to quarry-edge with the run's grant so each action is still grant-checked, approved and receipted per Quarry step. Ship with opaque handles, no imports and freeze-and-copy of every argument that reaches an approval or Quarry call.
whyItMatters: Fewer model round-trips and tokens for multi-step tasks (fill a form, paginate, extract a table), and programmatic post-processing of page data before it reaches the model. It preserves 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' because each host call is a Quarry step.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (one persistent QuickJS scope per session with a small surface: page, tabs, snapshot, annotatedScreenshot, fetch, plus runtime lints; AA083 non-marshalable host handles)
others: Codex (CA077/CA054 model-visible vs programmatic observation split; approval inputs copied into a frozen object to close a TOCTOU gap)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Embed a WASM JS engine with memory/stack limits and an interrupt deadline; keep one top-level scope per session; inject host functions that marshal to typed commands; return only values the script emits to the model. Before any approval, verify arguments are plain own data properties, deep-copy, freeze and execute exactly the frozen copy; reject module import/require.

verevonToday.gap: Verevon exposes browser.observe / browser.act as one typed action per model call; there is no batching and no programmatic post-processing. Hardening is only relevant once code-mode exists; typed JSON actions are already plain data.

approach: Model Plane sandboxes/execution-core: isolate runtime with typed bindings that are thin clients for quarry-edge /step using the run's grant; approvals stay per Quarry step, not per script. Build only after the single-step loop (R-t2-09-02) is live and measured, so token and latency data justifies it.
risks: Larger attack surface from model-written code; shipping without the hardening would create approval bypasses; one script can contain many actions, so per-script approval is unsafe.

verevon.exactGap: No script runtime exists: execution-core offers browser.observe and browser.act as single typed JSON actions (closed oneOf schema, additionalProperties false, snapshot refs only, no JavaScript, CSS selector or URL) and a bwrap-sandboxed code_interpreter that runs only python or sh with no network and no tool bridge. Code-mode is planned generically in Model Plane docs only (MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md sections 23.4-23.5 and verevon_CHAT_PARITY_BACKLOG.md #11, an in-sandbox RPC client), with no browser-specific design and no code, so the item's alreadyPlanned=false is inaccurate. The approval-input hardening half has no present gap: typed browser.act input is plain data and the approval stores the exact tool_input in a frozen, encrypted continuation descriptor.

verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: every binding call stays a separate Quarry step with the run's grant and its own approval; one approval must never cover a whole script. Approvals are durable pauses with an exact frozen descriptor and browser_agent cannot be cold-resumed, so a script waiting on approval must keep its sandbox alive and end as unknown-outcome when the wait budget is exceeded. ZDR: script inputs and outputs must not be persisted and must be scrubbed like code_interpreter output. Code-mode in general is already planned in Model Plane docs, so this must be a slice of that effort, not a parallel runtime. Preconditions are unbuilt: browser grants have no issuance path and the single-step planner loop has not been measured.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Fold into the planned generic code-mode (docs 23.4/23.5, backlog #11) as one browser binding set. Run the engine as a bwrap'd child of execution-core with network disabled, speaking a line-delimited RPC to the parent, which proxies each binding to browser.observe/browser.act with approvals, instead of embedding QuickJS or V8 in the execution-core process. Python over RPC (backlog #11) is the lower-risk first engine because code_interpreter already ships it; choose JavaScript only for a measured reason. Drop freeze-and-copy hardening from scope until a script can reach an approval, since the typed schema and descriptor already provide it.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. The sandbox substrate exists, but the item depends on grant issuance and a measured single-step loop; it becomes XL if a new JavaScript engine is embedded in-process.
verevon.verdictReason: Code-mode is already planned generically, the browser variant has unbuilt preconditions (grants, planner loop, measurements) and unproven savings, and the proposed in-process isolate conflicts with the existing sandboxed-child pattern. Keep as a later slice of the generic code-mode work.
